entries.name: AlertDialog — Loading
entries.description: A confirmation dialog that shows a spinner while the action runs.

entries.name: AlertDialog — Delete
entries.description: A delete button that asks the user to confirm before deleting.

entries.name: AppShell — Content Only
entries.description: Minimal shell with no navigation, useful for full-bleed pages, auth screens, or embedded views.

entries.name: useAppShellMobile — Custom Mobile Trigger
entries.description: Custom mobile navigation trigger built with useAppShellMobile. The trigger consumes the surrounding AppShell context instead of rendering its own shell.

entries.name: App Shell
entries.description: A basic app shell with content padding.

entries.name: AppShell — Side Nav Only
entries.description: App shell with SideNav header providing app identity, no TopNav needed.

entries.name: AppShell — Top Nav Only
entries.description: Simple layout with TopNav and no side navigation, suitable for landing pages.

entries.name: AppShell — Top Nav with Side Nav
entries.description: The most common layout with TopNav for app identity and SideNav for page-level navigation.

entries.name: AppShell — With Banner
entries.description: Full layout with TopNav, SideNav, and a dismissable info banner between the nav and content.

entries.name: AspectRatio — Circle Image
entries.description: Circular container via shape="ellipse" with ratio={1}, ideal for avatars and profile images.

entries.name: AspectRatio — Image Gallery
entries.description: Grid of images with consistent 4:3 aspect ratios.

entries.name: Aspect Ratio
entries.description: Three aspect ratio containers at equal height (1:1, 4:3, and 16:9), each showing an image with its ratio labeled below.

entries.name: AspectRatio — Square Image
entries.description: 1:1 square aspect ratio, ideal for avatars and Instagram-style images.

entries.name: AspectRatio — 16:9 Widescreen Image
entries.description: 16:9 widescreen aspect ratio wrapping an image.

entries.name: AspectRatio — Loading Skeleton
entries.description: Aspect ratio container with a skeleton loading placeholder.

entries.name: Avatar — Fallback Chain
entries.description: Demonstrates the avatar fallback chain: primary image, fallback image, initials, then default icon.

entries.name: Avatar — Group
entries.description: Overlap multiple avatars in a row to represent a group of people. Use for team lists, PR reviewers, or participant counts where you want to show faces without taking up much space.

entries.name: Avatar Group — Interactive
entries.description: A facepile whose avatars link to profiles, with an overflow indicator that opens the full member list. The whole group is one Tab stop; arrow keys move between the avatars and the overflow button.

entries.name: Avatar Group Overflow — Custom Text
entries.description: Provide short custom children such as 12+ when the overflow count needs compact product-specific formatting.

entries.name: Avatar Group Overflow — Default Count
entries.description: Use AvatarGroupOverflow without children to render the standard +N overflow count.

entries.name: Avatar Group Overflow
entries.description: Overflow indicators for hidden avatars, including the default +N label and custom count text.

entries.name: Avatar Group
entries.description: Overlapping avatar rows with a sliced visible set and a server-side overflow count. Shows team members in a compact facepile layout.

entries.name: Avatar — Initials
entries.description: Show initials instead of a photo. The avatar extracts the first and last initials from the name automatically. Use when you only have a user name, like in anonymous accounts or new user onboarding.

entries.name: Avatar — Interactive
entries.description: Make an avatar interactive by passing `href` to render it as a link or `onClick` to render it as a button. Both forms are focusable and show a focus-visible ring for keyboard users. Use for profile links, mention pop-ups, or any avatar people can act on.

entries.name: Avatar
entries.description: Avatars at every size with an image, initials fallback, and a status dot. A quick visual reference for choosing the right size.

entries.name: Avatar Status Dot
entries.description: AvatarStatusDot renders a presence indicator on an Avatar, with variants for positive, neutral, and negative states. The dot size automatically coordinates with the Avatar size.

entries.name: AvatarStatusDot — Variants
entries.description: Presence dots on Avatars using the success, neutral, and error variants. Pass an AvatarStatusDot to the Avatar status prop; the dot sizes itself to match the Avatar.

entries.name: Avatar — Tooltip
entries.description: By default an avatar shows its name in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. Pass a string to show custom text instead, or false to turn the tooltip off.

entries.name: Avatar — User Card
entries.description: Place an avatar next to a name and role to create a user card row. Use for comment headers, contact lists, profile sections, or anywhere you need to identify a person at a glance.

entries.name: Avatar — Photo
entries.description: Show a profile photo at different sizes. Use when you have a user photo URL. If the image fails to load, initials are shown instead.

entries.name: Avatar — Status Dot
entries.description: Add a status dot to an avatar to show whether someone is online, away, or busy. Use in chat, messaging, or any UI where knowing availability matters.

entries.name: Badge — Colors
entries.description: Tag items with color-coded categories like teams, priorities, or topics. Use the 9 non-semantic color variants when you need to distinguish groups visually.

entries.name: Badge — Counts
entries.description: Show a number inside a badge for notification counts, unread messages, or task totals. Use next to icons, nav items, or list labels.

entries.name: Badge — Variants
entries.description: All semantic and color badge variants in a single view. Use semantic variants for status and color variants for categories.

entries.name: Badge — Status
entries.description: Show the state of an item like Active, Pending, or Failed. Use in table rows, list items, or detail pages where users need to see status at a glance.

entries.name: Banner — Collapsible
entries.description: Combine an action button, dismiss control, and a collapsible detail area in one banner. Children sit behind the toggle by default; `collapsible={{defaultIsOpen: true}}` starts it open, and `collapsible={false}` drops the toggle entirely. Use for complex notifications like config changes or deployment summaries.

entries.name: Banner — Dismiss
entries.description: Let the user close a banner after reading it. Use for maintenance notices, feature tips, or any non-critical message the user can acknowledge.

entries.name: Banner — Floating
entries.description: A floating banner raised with `elevation="med"`. Banners are inline by default; raise one when it should read as an overlay above content.

entries.name: Banner — Full Width
entries.description: A full-width banner with no border radius for page-level notifications. Use at the top of a page for site-wide announcements or maintenance alerts.

entries.name: Banner — Statuses
entries.description: All four status banners stacked: info, success, warning, and error. A quick visual reference for choosing the right status.

entries.name: Banner — Statuses
entries.description: All 4 banner statuses: info, success, warning, and error. Use to show persistent messages like updates, confirmations, cautions, or problems at the top of a page or section.

entries.name: Banner — Action
entries.description: Add a button to a banner so the user can act on the message. Use for trial expirations, payment failures, or anything that needs a response.

entries.name: BaseTypeahead — Custom Search Bar
entries.description: BaseTypeahead embedded inside a custom-styled wrapper. The wrapper provides its own border and icon chrome; anchorRef positions the dropdown relative to it. Use this pattern when Typeahead's built-in field layout does not fit your composition.

entries.name: Base Typeahead
entries.description: A custom result renderer that adds supporting metadata while BaseTypeahead retains option semantics and keyboard behavior.

entries.name: Blockquote — Showcase
entries.description: Blockquote with and without citation. A quick visual reference for the blockquote component.

entries.name: Blockquote — Testimonials
entries.description: Multiple quotes arranged in a card grid for a testimonials section. Combine with Card and Grid to create social-proof layouts.

entries.name: Blockquote — With Attribution
entries.description: A plain quote and a quote with a cite attribution. Use cite to credit the original author or source.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet — Height variants
entries.description: Compares hug, capped, and tall starting heights for different amounts of content.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet — Mobile keyboard
entries.description: Uses a tall, scrollable form that keeps focused controls visible above the mobile keyboard.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet — No scrim
entries.description: Keeps the page visible and interactive behind a non-modal bottom sheet.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet
entries.description: A mobile filter surface that rises from the bottom edge.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet — Snap points
entries.description: Drag-to-resize stops: a half-height working surface, and a peek that slides away and thins the scrim.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet Switcher — Review flow
entries.description: A two-step form flow that lets a person review settings, confirm them, or move back without replacing the shared dialog.

entries.name: Bottom Sheet Switcher
entries.description: A three-step flow that transitions between content-hugging sheets of different heights inside one shared dialog.

entries.name: BreadcrumbItem — Basic
entries.description: Breadcrumb links inside a Breadcrumbs trail. Ancestor pages get an href; mark the last item with isCurrent to render it as plain text for the current page.

entries.name: Breadcrumb Item
entries.description: BreadcrumbItem represents a single step in a breadcrumb trail, supporting links, icons, current-page markers, and custom link components.

entries.name: Breadcrumbs — Separators
entries.description: Swap the default "/" for a different character like chevrons, arrows, or dots. Use when the visual style of the page calls for a different separator.

entries.name: Breadcrumbs — Deep Path
entries.description: A 5-level breadcrumb trail for deeply nested content. Use in e-commerce, file browsers, or any UI with several levels of hierarchy.

entries.name: Breadcrumbs — Menu item
entries.description: Give a mid-trail crumb a `menu` prop to turn it into a menu trigger for switching between sibling destinations. It reuses the same item API as DropdownMenu, so an existing option array (or composed item children) drops in verbatim.

entries.name: Breadcrumbs
entries.description: A breadcrumb trail showing page hierarchy with linked ancestors and a current page.

entries.name: Breadcrumbs — Variants
entries.description: Compare the default and supporting variants side by side. Use the supporting variant in dense UIs like admin panels where the breadcrumb should be subtle.

entries.name: Breadcrumbs — Icons
entries.description: Add icons before breadcrumb labels for quick recognition. Use a home icon on the root item and contextual icons on key sections.

entries.name: Button — Floating
entries.description: A floating action button raised with `elevation="med"`. Use elevation for buttons that hover above content, like a FAB.

entries.name: ButtonGroup — Basic
entries.description: Three related actions joined into a single connected control. Provide a group label for accessibility and keep all buttons the same variant so they read as one unit.

entries.name: ButtonGroup — Floating
entries.description: A grouped action bar raised with `elevation="med"`. The connected buttons share one surface, so the shadow lifts them as a unit.

entries.name: Button — Variants
entries.description: All four button variants side by side: primary, secondary, ghost, and destructive. A quick visual reference for choosing the right variant.

entries.name: Button — Sizes
entries.description: Small, medium, and large buttons side by side. Use small in dense UIs like toolbars, medium for most cases, and large for prominent CTAs.

entries.name: Button — Variants
entries.description: All 4 button variants in default, disabled, and loading states. Use primary for the main action, secondary for most others, ghost for low-emphasis, and destructive for dangerous actions.

entries.name: Button — End Slot
entries.description: Buttons with a trailing badge showing a count or status. Use for notification counts, unread messages, or any button that needs a visual indicator.

entries.name: Button — Icon
entries.description: Buttons with a leading icon that reinforces the label. Use when the icon helps the user identify the action faster, like a plus for "New" or a trash can for "Delete".

entries.name: Calendar — Constraints
entries.description: Limit which dates can be selected using min/max bounds and custom rules like weekdays only. Use for scheduling UIs where certain dates are unavailable.

entries.name: Calendar — Range
entries.description: Pick a start and end date with the range highlighted between them. Use for booking dates, time-off requests, or report filters.

entries.name: Calendar
entries.description: An interactive single-date calendar with a selected date. Click any day to change the selection.

entries.name: Calendar — Single
entries.description: Pick one date from a month grid. Use for appointment dates, due dates, or any field that needs a single date.

entries.name: Calendar — Two Months
entries.description: Two months side by side for selecting ranges that span a month boundary. Use in booking or travel UIs where check-in and check-out often fall in different months.

entries.name: Card — Callout
entries.description: Muted-variant cards for tips, notes, or supplementary information. Use when content should be visually distinct but not prominent. The muted variant uses a wash background instead of the elevated default, making it feel recessed rather than raised. Works well in sidebars, help panels, or inline callouts.

entries.name: Card — Elevations
entries.description: The four elevation levels side by side. Cards are flat by default; raise a card with `elevation` only when it needs to float above surrounding content.

entries.name: Card
entries.description: A card with a heading and body text showing the default container style.

entries.name: Card — Variants
entries.description: Default, muted, and color variants side by side. Use color variants to categorize cards visually, like team colors, project tags, or content types. Each color uses the corresponding background token from the theme, so they adapt to light and dark mode automatically.

entries.name: Card — Layout
entries.description: A card with a structured header, content area, and footer with action buttons. Use for forms, dialogs, or settings panels that need clear sections. Pair Card with Layout to get automatic dividers between header, content, and footer. The footer aligns actions to the right by default.

entries.name: Card — Simple
entries.description: A card with a heading and body text. Use for summaries, descriptions, or any grouped content that needs visual separation from the page. The card handles its own border, background, and padding; just pass your content as children. Set a width to constrain it, or leave it to fill the parent.

entries.name: Carousel — Cards
entries.description: A horizontally scrollable row of cards with snap scrolling enabled. Use for feature grids, product lists, or any set of cards that overflows the available width. The carousel adds fade edges and navigation buttons automatically.

entries.name: Carousel
entries.description: A horizontal carousel of cards with scroll-snap and navigation buttons. Scroll or click the arrows to browse.

entries.name: Carousel — Snap
entries.description: Scroll-snap carousel with navigation buttons and team member cards. Each card snaps to the start edge on scroll. Use when items should be viewed one at a time rather than as a continuous strip.

entries.name: Center — Horizontal Center
entries.description: A formatting control group centered with axis="horizontal" in the default horizontal writing mode. In other writing modes, Center currently follows the flex main axis rather than guaranteeing physical horizontal centering.

entries.name: Center — Vertical & Horizontal Center
entries.description: An empty state with an icon, heading, and description centered both vertically and horizontally inside a card. This is the most common use of Center: placing content in the middle of a fixed-height area like a panel, card, or content region. The height prop defines the centering space.

entries.name: Center
entries.description: Content centered horizontally and vertically inside a fixed-height container.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Attachments
entries.description: Chat composer with removable file tokens in a collapsible drawer. Use when users can attach files or context to their message.

entries.name: ChatComposerDrawer — Attachments
entries.description: Drawer with two rows: a scrollable carousel of image thumbnails and a row of removable file tokens. Omit count to keep the drawer always expanded.

entries.name: ChatComposerDrawer — Collapsible
entries.description: Drawer with many items and a collapse toggle. Pass count to enable the toggle; collapsed state shows a badge with the total count and a label.

entries.name: ChatComposerDrawer — Feedback
entries.description: Chat composer drawer with a feedback prompt and selectable lettered options. Use for user confirmation workflows that require explicit action before proceeding.

entries.name: Chat Composer Drawer
entries.description: Composer drawer with file tokens, a collapsible toggle, and header actions. Use as a starting point for any chat composer with attachments.

entries.name: ChatComposerDrawer — With Progress
entries.description: Drawer paired with a context progress bar in the header. Show context window usage when attachments consume part of the available token budget.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Flat
entries.description: The composer is raised by default (`elevation="low"`). Set `elevation="none"` to flatten it; it then draws a border with the same rest / hover / focus treatment as a text input.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Footer Actions
entries.description: Chat composer with dropdown menus for a model selector and settings in the footer, and a mic button in the send actions slot.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Full Featured
entries.description: Chat composer with all slots populated: collapsible attachment drawer, header actions, context progress bar, footer dropdown menus, and mic button. Shows the maximum composer configuration.

entries.name: ChatComposerInput — Controlled
entries.description: Controlled chat input with live value display. Use controlled mode when you need to read or transform the input value outside the composer.

entries.name: ChatComposerInput — Disabled
entries.description: Composer in a disabled state. Use when the input should be visible but not interactive, such as during streaming or when a prerequisite is unmet.

entries.name: ChatComposerInput — Mentions
entries.description: Chat input with an @ trigger that opens a typeahead menu for mentioning users. Selected names appear as inline tokens.

entries.name: ChatComposerInput — Multiple Triggers
entries.description: Chat input with both @ mentions and / commands. Each trigger type renders tokens in a distinct color so users can tell them apart at a glance.

entries.name: ChatComposerInput — Slash Commands
entries.description: Chat input with a / trigger for command selection. Use for AI assistants or bots that support structured commands.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Simple
entries.description: Minimal chat composer with a placeholder and submit handler. The simplest way to drop a message input into a page.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Streaming
entries.description: Chat composer with streaming state and a stop button. Use when the assistant is generating a response and the user can cancel.

entries.name: ChatComposer — Validation
entries.description: Chat composer with error and warning status messages. Status can appear above or below the composer to surface validation or system feedback.

entries.name: ChatDictationButton — Basic
entries.description: A dictation button wired to useChatDictation and placed in the sendActions slot of a ChatComposer. Click the microphone to transcribe speech into the input.

entries.name: Chat Dictation Button
entries.description: Interactive dictation button connected to the SpeechRecognition API via useChatDictation. Click the mic to dictate into the composer.

entries.name: ChatDictationButton — In Composer
entries.description: Dictation button placed in the sendActions slot of a chat composer. Shows the recommended integration point for voice input alongside the send button.

entries.name: ChatDictationButton — States
entries.description: Dictation button in idle, listening, and speaking states side by side. Shows the three visual phases of a voice input interaction.

entries.name: ChatDictationButton — Sizes
entries.description: Small and medium dictation buttons side by side. Use small in compact composer densities and medium for standard layouts.

entries.name: ChatLayout — Panel View
entries.description: Narrow sidebar chat in a constrained container that triggers compact density. Use for side panels, drawers, or embedded chat widgets where horizontal space is limited.

entries.name: ChatLayoutScrollButton — Labels
entries.description: Scroll button with different labels for context-specific notifications like new messages, unread replies, or a generic scroll prompt.

entries.name: Chat Layout Scroll Button
entries.description: Scroll button in hidden, visible, and expanded (with label) states. The button fades in when the user scrolls up and expands when new messages arrive.

entries.name: ChatMessage — Avatar & Name
entries.description: Messages with avatars and sender names. Place the name on the bubble when using bubbles, or on the message wrapper for raw content.

entries.name: ChatMessageBubble — Custom Content
entries.description: Custom in-message content aligned to the bubble text column. An artifact card is wrapped in a ghost bubble with width="100%", so its left edge matches the bubble text and it spans the full message column instead of the default bubble width cap; the timestamp rides the bubble metadata slot.

entries.name: ChatMessageBubble — Density
entries.description: Compact, balanced, and spacious density modes side by side. Density controls bubble padding, corner radius, and spacing between grouped bubbles.

entries.name: ChatMessageBubble — Grouping
entries.description: Multi-bubble messages using first, middle, and last group positions. Grouped bubbles tighten corner radius on the sender side for a continuous visual flow.

entries.name: ChatMessageBubble — Metadata
entries.description: Bubbles with name and metadata slots aligned to bubble padding. Put name on the first bubble and metadata on the last bubble in a message.

entries.name: Chat Message Bubble
entries.description: Grouped user bubbles with filled styling and a ghost-variant agent response, with timestamps and delivery status.

entries.name: ChatMessageBubble — Variants
entries.description: Filled and ghost bubble variants for both user and assistant senders. Use filled for standard messages and ghost when content needs alignment without a visual boundary.

entries.name: ChatMessage — Ghost
entries.description: Ghost variant for messages without visible bubble boundaries. Keeps padding for alignment but renders a transparent background, useful for AI-style responses.

entries.name: ChatMessageList — Density
entries.description: Side-by-side comparison of compact, balanced, and spacious densities. Use compact in sidebars or panels, balanced for most full-page chat, and spacious for long-form reading. Use gap when row spacing needs to differ from density.

entries.name: ChatMessageList — Full Featured
entries.description: Conversation showcasing system messages, multi-bubble grouping, markdown, code blocks, and metadata. Combines date dividers, ghost bubbles, grouped messages, and rich content in a single example.

entries.name: Chat Message List
entries.description: Basic AI chat conversation with user and assistant messages. The simplest way to render a message list with alternating sender bubbles, metadata, and a date divider.

entries.name: ChatMessageMetadata — Footer Actions
entries.description: Assistant message with footer actions: copy, retry, thumbs up/down, and model label. Use for AI responses that need feedback or utility controls.

entries.name: Chat Message Metadata
entries.description: Three-message conversation showcasing error status with retry, delivery status, and full footer actions with model label.

entries.name: ChatMessageMetadata — Status
entries.description: All 5 delivery statuses (sending, sent, delivered, read, and error), each with a timestamp. Use to show message delivery progress or surface failures.

entries.name: ChatMessageMetadata — Timestamps
entries.description: Timestamp-only metadata on user and assistant messages. Supports absolute time and relative formats via Timestamp.

entries.name: ChatMessage — Multi-Bubble
entries.description: Grouped bubbles using the group prop for corner radius reduction. Use first, middle, and last to visually connect related bubbles from the same sender.

entries.name: Chat Message
entries.description: A user multi-bubble group with delivery status and an assistant ghost response with avatar, name, timestamp, and model info.

entries.name: ChatSendButton — Custom Icon
entries.description: Send buttons with custom icons via sendIcon and stopIcon props. Use to match the personality of the chat experience: a paper airplane for messaging, sparkles for AI generation, or a check mark for confirmation flows.

entries.name: ChatSendButton — In Composer
entries.description: Send button inside ChatComposer, where it reads state from context automatically. No wiring needed; the button enables when the input has content.

entries.name: Chat Send Button
entries.description: Ready, custom icon, and streaming states of the send button.

entries.name: ChatSendButton — States
entries.description: Disabled, ready, and streaming states at both sizes. The button automatically toggles between send (primary) and stop (secondary) based on streaming state.

entries.name: Chat System Message
entries.description: System messages for date dividers, status updates, and informational notices. Shows both default and divider variants in a realistic conversation flow.

entries.name: ChatSystemMessage — Status Updates
entries.description: Realistic status messages in a conversation flow showing membership changes, timestamps, and resolution notices.

entries.name: ChatSystemMessage — Variants
entries.description: Default and divider variants side by side. Use default for inline status updates and divider for date separators or section breaks.

entries.name: ChatSystemMessage — Icon
entries.description: System messages with a leading icon that reinforces the message type. Use icons to help users scan and identify message categories at a glance.

entries.name: ChatTokenizedText — Basic
entries.description: A message with @mention tokens. Each matching pattern is replaced with its display name badge.

entries.name: ChatTokenizedText — Colors
entries.description: Tokens with different color variants to distinguish mentions, bugs, and features. Use variant colors to create a visual taxonomy: blue for people, red for bugs, green for features.

entries.name: ChatToolCalls — Expandable
entries.description: Tool calls with expandable result details showing diffs and command output in code blocks. Click a row to reveal its result.

entries.name: ChatToolCalls — Statuses
entries.description: All four status states (pending, running, complete, and error) shown together in a single group.

entries.name: ChatToolCalls — Simple
entries.description: A single inline tool call above a collapsible multi-call group with diff stats. Shows both layouts side by side.

entries.name: CheckboxInput — States
entries.description: Checkboxes with labels and descriptions in checked, unchecked, and disabled states. Each checkbox controls a single on/off setting. Add a description to explain what the setting does.

entries.name: CheckboxInput — Indeterminate
entries.description: A "select all" checkbox that controls a group of options. When only some options are checked, it shows a dash instead of a checkmark. Clicking it checks or unchecks everything.

entries.name: Checkbox Input
entries.description: Interactive checkboxes showing checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states with descriptions.

entries.name: CheckboxInput — Status
entries.description: Checkboxes with error, warning, and success validation messages. Use the status prop to show feedback after form validation: errors block submission, warnings inform, and success confirms.

entries.name: CheckboxListItem — Basic
entries.description: Checkbox items with labels and descriptions inside a controlled CheckboxList. Use for multi-select option groups like notification preferences.

entries.name: Checkbox List Item
entries.description: Checkbox list items with labels, descriptions, and different states including disabled.

entries.name: CheckboxList — Select All With Indeterminate
entries.description: A "select all" toggle at the top of a checkbox list that switches to an indeterminate dash when only some items are checked, useful for bulk actions like exporting documents or assigning permissions where users often want everything at once.

entries.name: CheckboxList — With End Content
entries.description: Badges in the trailing slot show contextual info, like a price or status, next to each option without cluttering the label, so users can compare choices at a glance.

entries.name: Citation — Inline Text
entries.description: Citations embedded within a paragraph of text, showing how they flow inline with surrounding content.

entries.name: Citation — Showcase
entries.description: All citation variants at a glance: label chips and numbered badges, with and without icons and links.

entries.name: Citation — Source List
entries.description: A list of citation sources with icons, as you might show at the end of an AI-generated response or article footer.

entries.name: Clickable Card — Elevated
entries.description: A clickable card raised with `elevation="med"` so the shadow signals the whole surface is interactive.

entries.name: Clickable Card
entries.description: A clickable card that navigates on click. Nested interactive elements work independently.

entries.name: Clickable Card — Nested Button
entries.description: A product card that navigates on click but has an independent "Add to cart" button inside.

entries.name: Code — Text Sizes
entries.description: Inline code rendered inside heading, body, supporting, and label text. Code automatically matches the font size of its parent text element.

entries.name: Code — Snippet
entries.description: Short terminal commands with a copy button and no line numbers. Use for install instructions or one-liner commands that readers will paste directly.

entries.name: Code — Highlighted
entries.description: TypeScript code with specific lines highlighted to draw attention to a key section. Use highlightLines to call out new or important code in tutorials and changelogs.

entries.name: Code — Config
entries.description: A JSON configuration file with a title bar and line numbers. The title prop adds a filename label in the header so readers know which file the code belongs to.

entries.name: Code — Scrollable
entries.description: A long code block with a max height that enables vertical scrolling. Use maxHeight to keep the block from dominating the page when displaying large files.

entries.name: Code Block
entries.description: A syntax-highlighted TypeScript code block with line numbers, a title bar, and a copy button.

entries.name: Code — Terminal
entries.description: A dark terminal-style command block: a bash CodeBlock wrapped in SyntaxTheme with the GitHub Dark preset, copy button on, and no line numbers. Use for shell sessions or CLI output that should read as a terminal even on light pages. Reach for a dark syntax preset instead of hand-rolling a dark box with custom CSS.

entries.name: Code — Inline
entries.description: Inline code references mixed within a paragraph of body text. Use Code to mark up function names, hooks, or API terms so they stand out from surrounding prose.

entries.name: Code
entries.description: Inline code snippets inside a sentence showing how Code renders alongside body text.

entries.name: Code — Content Types
entries.description: Inline code used for variables, terminal commands, CSS properties, file paths, and keyboard shortcuts. Shows how Code adapts to different kinds of technical content.

entries.name: Collapsible — Controlled
entries.description: Manage the open section from parent state, so something other than a click can move it: a URL parameter, a form jumping to the step that failed validation, or the Previous/Next controls shown here. onChange hands back the whole open value.

entries.name: Collapsible — FAQ
entries.description: FAQ built with hasDividers: row hairlines and density padding with no custom CSS. Questions set their own type — body at semibold, not the trigger's default 17px large — so a list of questions reads as rows rather than a stack of headings, and question and answer separate on weight and color instead of size.

entries.name: CollapsibleGroup — Density
entries.description: density sets the block padding on every row in the group, so a list of sections can be tuned to the surface it sits on without touching the rows. compact for dense surfaces like sidebars and inspectors, balanced (the default) for page content, spacious for a short list that is the main thing on the page. It follows Table's scale and pairs with hasDividers, which turns it on at balanced.

entries.name: Collapsible Group
entries.description: CollapsibleGroup coordinates its Collapsible children: with type="single", opening one closes the others. No state or handlers in the example — the group owns which value is open and each child only declares its own. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its default large type as the heading of its own surface.

entries.name: useCollapsible — Custom Disclosure
entries.description: Custom disclosure UI built directly with useCollapsible for headless open/close state.

entries.name: Collapsible — Multiple Mode
entries.description: Several sections open at once, for comparing across them — feature lists, pricing tiers. One Collapsible per Card, so each trigger keeps its own large type: it is the heading of its surface, not a row in a list.

entries.name: Collapsible

entries.description: Only one section open at a time, so a single body of content competes for attention. Use defaultValue to pre-expand whichever section a first-time reader needs. Each Collapsible owns a Section, so its trigger is that section heading.

entries.name: Collapsible — With Dividers
entries.description: A flat list on the page background with hand-placed Dividers, for detail panels and sidebars where cards would add too much weight. Rows, so the triggers step down to body-semibold and a supporting metadata line sits under each answer.

entries.name: useTableColumnResize — Draggable Columns

entries.name: CommandPalette — Async Search

entries.name: CommandPalette — Grouped

entries.name: CommandPalette — Custom Footer
entries.description: Command palette with a custom footer tip message.

entries.name: CommandPaletteEmpty — Basic

entries.name: Command Palette Empty
entries.description: Command palette empty state shown when no commands are available.

entries.name: CommandPaletteFooter — Basic
entries.description: A command palette footer with no children, rendering the built-in keyboard navigation hints. Use CommandPaletteFooter without content to get the default arrow-key, Enter, and Esc hints below the results list.

entries.name: Command Palette Footer
entries.description: Command palette footer with custom tip content.

entries.name: CommandPaletteGroup — Basic
entries.description: Command palette items organized under group headings using the composed CommandPaletteGroup form. Use to separate related commands into labeled sections.

entries.name: Command Palette Group
entries.description: Command palette groups in both data-driven (auxiliaryData.group) and composed (CommandPaletteGroup + CommandPaletteItem) forms.

entries.name: CommandPaletteInput — With End Content
entries.description: Custom placeholder and a keyboard shortcut badge in the trailing slot via endContent.

entries.name: Command Palette Input
entries.description: Command palette search input with a custom placeholder and a keyboard shortcut hint in the endContent slot.

entries.name: CommandPaletteItem — Basic
entries.description: Selectable command palette items inside a CommandPaletteList, including highlighted and disabled states. Use when composing a palette manually instead of a search source.

entries.name: Command Palette Item
entries.description: Command palette items with custom content via renderItem and as composed CommandPaletteItem with icons, highlighted, selected, and disabled states.

entries.name: CommandPaletteList — Item States

entries.name: Command Palette List
entries.description: Scrollable command palette list with grouped items, including a highlighted item, composed without a full CommandPalette.

entries.name: CommandPalette — Picker Mode
entries.description: Single-value picker with persistent selection and check indicator.

entries.name: CommandPalette — Rich Items
entries.description: Custom item rendering with icons, keyboard shortcuts, and keyword search.

entries.name: Command Palette
entries.description: Basic command palette with static items and keyboard navigation.

entries.name: Complex Selector — Deadline Picker
entries.description: A multi-step deadline field: pick a preset like Today or Next week, or switch to a custom date and time before applying. The popup stays open until the user commits, so the content owns the Apply action.

entries.name: Complex Selector
entries.description: A two-axis picker: choose a fruit and a ripeness level from one control. ComplexSelector owns the trigger, popover, and focus restore while the custom grid owns its keyboard semantics.

entries.name: Complex Selector — Tree Search
entries.description: A destination picker that combines a search field with a TreeList hierarchy. TreeList owns tree keyboard navigation; ComplexSelector owns the trigger, popover, and focus restore. Selecting a folder closes the popup.

entries.name: ContextMenu — Basic
entries.description: An adaptive context area: long-press opens a BottomSheet on compact touch screens, while right-click opens a cursor-positioned menu elsewhere.

entries.name: ContextMenu — Bottom Sheet
entries.description: A ContextMenu using the explicit BottomSheet presentation. Long-press the target on touch devices or right-click it with a pointer. Keep a visible menu trigger for important mobile actions.

entries.name: ContextMenuItem — Basic
entries.description: Context menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use ContextMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.

entries.name: Context Menu Item
entries.description: Context menu with custom-rendered items using ContextMenuItem for icons and descriptions.

entries.name: Context Menu
entries.description: An adaptive context area that supports long-press on compact touch screens and right-click elsewhere.

entries.name: DateInput — Clearable
entries.description: Date input with a clear button that resets the value. Use when the date field is optional and the user may need to undo their selection.

entries.name: DateInput — Min/Max Constraints
entries.description: Date input constrained to a min/max window. Use when only certain dates are valid, like booking availability or a fiscal quarter.

entries.name: DateInput — Formats
entries.description: The format prop reuses Timestamp's format vocabulary to control how the committed value is displayed: date, date_long (default), date_weekday, and system_date, or a function for a fully custom string. Formatting applies only to the committed value, never to text the user is actively typing.

entries.name: Date Input
entries.description: A date input field with a calendar popover. Type a date or click the calendar icon to pick one.

entries.name: DateInput — Description
entries.description: Date input with helper text below the label explaining what the field expects. Use when the purpose of the date is not obvious from the label alone.

entries.name: DateInput — Validation
entries.description: Date input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface validation issues, caution the user, or confirm a valid selection.

entries.name: Date Range Input
entries.description: A date range picker with a button trigger and dual-month calendar popover with preset ranges.

entries.name: DateRangeInput — With Presets
entries.description: Date range picker with quick-select presets for common periods. Use for analytics dashboards, report filters, or any context where users frequently select standard time windows.

entries.name: DateRangeInput — Validation
entries.description: Date range input in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface booking conflicts, flag high-demand periods, or confirm an available range.

entries.name: Date Time Input
entries.description: A combined date and time picker. Desktop opens a calendar popover with a time input; touch devices open a Date/Time bottom sheet.

entries.name: DateTimeInput — Validation
entries.description: DateTimeInput in all three status states: error, warning, and success. Use to surface scheduling conflicts, caution the user about edge cases, or confirm a valid datetime.

entries.name: Dialog — Adaptive presentation
entries.description: Opt-in recipe for an AdaptiveDialog wrapper: Dialog remains the default everywhere, while touchPresentation="bottom-sheet" switches only at lg and below when pointer is coarse and hover is unavailable. Includes a deterministic presentation override for tests/unusual environments and notes that BottomSheet purpose controls swipe and scrim dismissal. Usage examples: touchPresentation="dialog" keeps Dialog, "fullscreen" chooses fullscreen Dialog, and "bottom-sheet" chooses BottomSheet only for the touch-oriented range. Keep presentation as the deterministic override. Do not use this by default for AlertDialog or destructive confirmations.

entries.name: Dialog — Confirmation
entries.description: Asks the user to confirm a destructive action before it happens. Use before deleting projects, removing team members, revoking API keys, or any irreversible operation.

entries.name: Dialog — Form
entries.description: Collects user input without navigating away from the page. Uses purpose="form" so clicking the backdrop won't close it. Use for editing profiles, creating items, or updating settings inline.

entries.name: Dialog — Fullscreen
entries.description: Takes over the entire viewport for content that needs maximum space. Use for documentation viewers, rich text editors, multi-step wizards, or media previews where the standard dialog width is too narrow.

entries.name: DialogHeader — Basic
entries.description: A DialogHeader with a title, subtitle, and close button, placed in the header slot of a Dialog Layout. Pass onOpenChange to render the close button.

entries.name: Dialog Header
entries.description: DialogHeader provides a structured header for dialogs with slots for title, subtitle, close button, and optional start or end content.

entries.name: Dialog — Scrollable
entries.description: Constrains the dialog height and scrolls the body when content overflows. Use for terms and conditions, license agreements, changelogs, or any long-form content the user needs to review before accepting.

entries.name: Dialog
entries.description: Modal dialog with a header, body content, and close button.

entries.name: Dialog — Required
entries.description: Cannot be dismissed by Escape or backdrop click; the user must explicitly choose an action. Uses purpose="required". Use for ownership transfers, legal acknowledgements, or critical decisions where skipping is not an option.

entries.name: Divider — Full Bleed
entries.description: Divider that extends past container padding to span the full width. Use inside cards or panels when you want a clean edge-to-edge separation, like between an order summary and total.

entries.name: Divider — Variants
entries.description: Horizontal dividers in subtle and strong variants, plus a labeled divider. A quick visual reference for separator styles.

entries.name: Divider — Variants
entries.description: Subtle, labeled, and strong dividers in a single card. Use subtle between related sections, labeled for alternatives like "or", and strong for high-contrast boundaries.

entries.name: Divider — Vertical
entries.description: Vertical dividers separating side-by-side metrics. Use between stat cards, toolbar groups, or any horizontal layout where you need a visual boundary between sections.

entries.name: DropdownMenu — Actions
entries.description: Action menu with dividers separating safe and destructive operations. Use for row-level actions on items like documents, projects, or records.

entries.name: DropdownMenu — Adaptive presentation
entries.description: Chooses a bottom sheet for compact touch surfaces and an anchored popover otherwise. The media query is product policy, while DropdownMenu owns both presentations.

entries.name: DropdownMenuItem — Basic
entries.description: Dropdown menu items with labels and secondary descriptions. Use DropdownMenuItem to render custom menu entries with consistent styling.

entries.name: Dropdown Menu Item
entries.description: Dropdown menu with custom-rendered items using DropdownMenuItem for icons and descriptions.

entries.name: DropdownMenu — Icon Trigger
entries.description: Overflow menu triggered by an icon-only button with no chevron or label text. Use for row-level actions in tables, cards, or lists where a text button would take too much space.

entries.name: Dropdown Menu
entries.description: A button that opens a dropdown menu with action items. The menu starts open for preview.

entries.name: DropdownMenu — Disabled
entries.description: Menu with selectively disabled items based on permissions. Use when some actions require higher privileges, like admin-only operations.

entries.name: DropdownMenu — Sections
entries.description: Menu items organized into titled sections for easy scanning. Use when you have 6+ actions that fall into distinct categories, like Create vs Manage.

entries.name: DropdownMenu — Submenu
entries.description: Action menu with a nested submenu. Hover or Right arrow opens the flyout; Left arrow / Escape closes it. Use to group related destinations or secondary actions without crowding the top level.

entries.name: EmptyState — Actions
entries.description: Full empty state with icon, message, and action buttons. Use when a search returns no results, a filter clears all items, or a list has been emptied. The buttons give the user a way forward: go back, clear filters, or try a different query.

entries.name: EmptyState — Compact
entries.description: Smaller empty state with reduced spacing for constrained areas. Use inside sidebar panels, card widgets, or notification drawers where a full-size empty state would overwhelm the layout.

entries.name: EmptyState — Container
entries.description: Empty state wrapped in a Card for first-time setup or onboarding. Use when the user has not created any items yet, like a project list, team roster, or dashboard widget that will fill with data once they take action.

entries.name: Empty State
entries.description: A no-results empty state with an icon, descriptive message, and a call-to-action button.

entries.name: FieldLabel — Basic
entries.description: Standalone labels with required and optional indicators and a helper description. Use when labeling a custom control that does not render its own label.

entries.name: Field Label

entries.name: Field — Required & Optional

entries.name: Field

entries.name: FieldStatus — Basic

entries.name: Field Status
entries.description: Field status messages in error, warning, and success states with attached and detached variants.

entries.name: Field — Validation States
entries.description: All three validation states: error, warning, and success. Use error for invalid input, warning for potential issues like reserved names, and success to confirm valid entries like API keys.

entries.name: Field — Description
entries.description: Fields with helper text below the label. Use descriptions to explain format requirements, constraints, or what happens with the data, like "At least 8 characters" or "We will send a confirmation link".

entries.name: FileInput — Basic

entries.name: FormLayout — Nested Address Form

entries.name: Form Layout
entries.description: A vertical form layout with text input fields.

entries.name: Grid — Dashboard Layout

entries.name: Grid — Card Gallery
entries.description: Card gallery with responsive columns that maintain consistent widths

entries.name: Grid — Responsive Auto-Fit

entries.name: Grid — Column Spanning

entries.description: Icon buttons that show a loading spinner on click for async feedback

entries.description: An icon button with a wrench icon.

entries.description: Icon buttons with tooltips that explain each action on hover

entries.description: Progress bar with its current percentage displayed.

entries.description: Raised selectable cards with `elevation="low"`. The inset selection ring composes on top of the shadow, so a selected card keeps its elevation.

entries.description: A plan picker with single-select radio behavior. Cards show an accent border when selected.

entries.name: Selector — Clearable
entries.description: Selector with a clear button to reset the selected value.

entries.name: Selector — Ghost Toolbar

entries.description: Options carry a description, so the dropdown draws a two-line row. entries.name: Selector Option
entries.description: Selector with custom-rendered options using SelectorOption for icons and descriptions.

entries.name: Selector — Grouped Sections
entries.description: Selector with options grouped into labeled sections.

entries.name: Selector — Validation States
entries.description: Selector showing error, warning, and success validation states.

entries.description: Place a collapse button in the SideNav footer to let users toggle the rail between expanded and collapsed states. Disable the built-in button via collapsible={{hasButton: false}} when positioning it yourself.

entries.name: Side Nav Collapse Button
entries.description: Demonstrates SideNavCollapseButton inside a collapsible SideNav.

entries.name: SideNav — End Content
entries.description: Side navigation items with badges, counts, and context menus as trailing content.

entries.name: SideNavHeading — Basic

entries.name: Side Nav Item

entries.description: Slider with custom formatting showing temperature in Fahrenheit.

entries.description: Default and onMedia shade spinners for light and dark backgrounds.

entries.description: A large spinner indicator.

entries.name: Spinner — Sizes

entries.name: Spinner — With Label
entries.description: Spinners with text and rich multi-line labels.

entries.description: Buttons positioned at the start, center, and end of a row.

entries.description: StackItem can be used within HStack or VStack for more granular control over individual item sizing and alignment, but is optional; stack children work without it.

entries.name: StatusDot — Pulsing
entries.description: Animated pulsing dots for live, processing, and error states.

entries.name: Status Dot
entries.description: A positive status dot indicator.

entries.name: StatusDot — Status Indicators
entries.description: Labeled status dot list for presence indicators like online, away, and offline.

entries.name: StatusDot — Variants
entries.description: All five semantic color variants displayed in a row.

entries.name: Step — Content Slot
entries.description: Children passed to a Step render below its description, indented to line up with the label rather than the indicator, and stay outside the clickable label area so buttons inside remain their own targets. In a full flow you gate the slot on the step being active. That is what turns a vertical stepper into an expanding one.

entries.name: Step — Indicator
entries.description: Everything the indicator prop accepts: the auto default, an always-number badge, a custom ReactNode, and none, each on its own completed Step so the prop is the only difference between them. Every variant occupies the same 16px box, so a step swapping its number for a check as it completes never shifts the label beside it. The last cell shows that a custom node can be live rather than static: a Spinner on a step that is in progress, shaded `inherit` so it picks up the step's own tint like any other glyph.

entries.name: Stepper — Custom Content
entries.description: A vertical stepper where each step owns a slice of the page. The content slot takes any node (form fields, a summary panel, a banner), so a stepper is not limited to multi-step forms. Rendering the slot only for the active step is what makes the flow expand one step at a time.

entries.name: Stepper — Indicator Modes
entries.description: The indicator prop side by side: none (the bar and label carry the progress on their own), auto (check when done, ring when current, number ahead), always-number, and a custom icon per step.

entries.name: Stepper — On-Track Horizontal
entries.description: The on-track layout in horizontal orientation: instead of sitting beside the label, each indicator is slotted into the connector itself, so the numbered nodes read as beads on one continuous line. Labels center under their node.

entries.name: Stepper — On-Track Vertical
entries.description: The on-track layout in vertical orientation: indicators sit inline on a continuous connector rail, with each label and description beside its node. Compare with the separated layout, where the indicator sits alongside its own bar segment instead of on a shared rail.

entries.name: Stepper — Checkout Progress
entries.description: The default stepper: a horizontal track where every step owns an equal segment of the progress bar above its label. The default auto indicator resolves itself per step: a check once the step is done, a ring on the current step, a number for the ones still ahead. Click any step to jump.

entries.name: Stepper — Validation Status
entries.description: Semantic status per step in a verification flow: success shows a green check, error a red glyph, accent the in-progress step. Status sets the indicator color and glyph only, never the connector, and is announced to assistive tech as text.

entries.name: Stepper — Horizontal Narrow Collapsed
entries.description: A narrow horizontal stepper using horizontalOptions. At 320px wide, four steps fall below the 112px minimumStepWidth and collapse into a current-step summary with Previous and Next controls.

entries.name: Step
entries.description: A single Step, with every part it can render: the indicator, the label with its optional marker and trailing endContent, and the description beneath. A Step never sets its own completed/current state. It declares its index and derives the rest from the parent Stepper, so one Step in one Stepper is a complete example.

entries.name: Step — States
entries.description: Every state a single Step can land in, each shown as one Step in its own Stepper. Completed, current, and upcoming are derived by comparing the step index against the parent activeStep, so they are never set directly; isDisabled and status are the two a step declares itself. Status is a separate axis from progress, which is why a completed step can still carry a warning.

entries.name: useTableStickyColumns — Pinned Columns
entries.description: A Table using useTableStickyColumns to pin the Name column to the start edge and Status to the end edge. Scroll horizontally; pinned columns stay in view with a soft shadow over the scrolling content.

entries.name: Switch — Disabled
entries.description: Disabled switch with label and description for gated features.

entries.description: Settings panel with spread-spaced switches in a card.

entries.description: Toggle with a label and supporting description text.

entries.name: Switch — With Status

entries.name: SyntaxTheme — Light Preset
entries.description: Use a light syntax preset for code examples that need to sit on light documentation surfaces.

entries.name: SyntaxTheme — Compact Preset
entries.description: A concise code block rendered with the One Dark Pro syntax preset to show how SyntaxTheme changes highlighting colors without making the page long.

entries.name: Table — Column Settings
entries.description: Table with a column visibility picker in the toolbar. Toggle columns on and off.

entries.name: Table — Popover Filters
entries.description: Table with popover filter controls triggered by icons in column headers.

entries.name: Table — Grid Dividers
entries.description: Compact table with grid dividers showing both row and column borders, suited for dense numeric data.

entries.name: useTableGroupedRows — Collapsible Groups
entries.description: A table grouped into collapsible sections with useTableGroupedRows. Each group gets a full-width header with a chevron, label, and member count; click to collapse/expand.

entries.name: Table — In Card
entries.description: Table composed inside a card with a heading, demonstrating container bleed alignment.

entries.name: Table — Inline Filters
entries.description: Table with inline filter controls rendered directly below each column header.

entries.name: Table — Paginated Data
entries.description: Paginated data table navigating through a larger dataset page by page.

entries.name: Table — Resizable Columns
entries.description: Table with draggable column resize handles. Drag the right edge of any header to resize.

entries.name: Table — Rich Cell Content
entries.description: Table with rich cell content using Link for emails and Badge for role labels.

entries.name: useTableRowExpansion — Tree Table
entries.description: A tree table using useTableRowExpansion with inherited columns. Child rows use the same columns as parents, indented by depth. Click the chevron or right-click to expand/collapse.

entries.name: useTableRowIndex — Numbered Rows
entries.description: A table with a prepended row-number column via useTableRowIndex. Numbering is monospaced, right-aligned, and follows the rendered data order.

entries.name: useTableRowStatus - Semantic and Custom Markers
entries.description: A job table using both row-status paths: status resolves themed semantic glyphs and tones, while color stays a custom paint choice with an optional caller-selected icon or the stable dot.

entries.name: Table — Row Selection
entries.description: Table with row selection checkboxes and a select-all header checkbox.

entries.name: Table
entries.description: Data-driven table with proportional and pixel column widths and hover highlighting.

entries.name: Table — Sortable Columns
entries.description: Table with sortable columns, click headers to sort ascending or descending.

entries.name: Table — Striped Rows
entries.description: Table with alternating row colors and hover highlighting for easy scanning.

entries.name: useTableTreeData: Tree Table
entries.description: A file-tree table built from nested data. useTableTreeState flattens the tree into the visible rows and owns the expanded set; useTableTreeData draws the per-level indent and the expand/collapse chevron in the tree column. The two hooks are designed to work together, so this one example covers both. hasExpandAllControl adds the expand-all/collapse-all toggle to the tree column header. Collapsed branches are unmounted, not hidden.

entries.name: TabList — Fill Layout
entries.description: Tabs that stretch to fill the available width with a bottom divider.

entries.name: TabList — With Actions
entries.description: Page header pattern with tabs on the left and action buttons pushed to the right. When hasDivider is true, match the Button size to the TabList size so the tabs and actions align to a shared baseline above the divider.

entries.name: TabList — With Badge
entries.description: Tabs with notification badge counts rendered via endContent. Uses error variant for urgent counts and neutral for informational ones.

entries.name: TabList — With Icons

entries.name: TabList — With Overflow Menu
entries.description: Tab list with a dropdown menu for additional items that do not fit inline.

entries.name: TabList — With Status Dot
entries.description: Tabs with status dot indicators rendered via endContent to show live environment health at a glance.

entries.name: Tab Menu
entries.description: TabMenu is an overflow menu within a TabList that groups additional tab options into a dropdown, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text.

entries.name: Tab
entries.description: Tab is an individual tab item within a TabList, supporting labels, icons, selected icons, and end content slots.

entries.description: All three status variants (error, warning, and success) with status messages, plus error without a message. Use to show inline validation feedback as the user types.

entries.name: TextArea — Icon
entries.description: Textareas with a leading icon that hints at the expected content, like a chat bubble for messages or a pencil for notes.

entries.name: Text — Colors
entries.description: All text color options (primary, secondary, disabled, placeholder, active) applied to body text to show their intended use.

entries.name: Text — Heading Levels
entries.description: All 6 heading levels (h1 through h6) rendered with Heading to show the full type scale.

entries.name: Text — Inline
entries.description: Mixing body and code text inline within a single line using the default inline display mode.

entries.name: TextInput — Icon
entries.description: Inputs with a leading icon that hints at the expected content. Use when the icon helps users identify the field faster, like a lock for passwords or an envelope for email.

entries.name: TextInput — Search
entries.description: Search input with a hidden label, start icon, and clear button. Use for toolbar and header search bars where the icon provides sufficient context.

entries.name: TextInput — Sizes
entries.description: Small, medium, and large inputs side by side. Use small in dense UIs like table filters, medium for most forms, and large for prominent single-field pages.

entries.name: TextInput — States
entries.description: Error, warning, and success validation states with status messages. Use to show users what went wrong and how to fix it.

entries.name: TextInput — Status variant
entries.description: The statusVariant prop controls whether the status message is attached to the bordered input (default, overlapping directly below) or detached from it (floating below as a separate element with spacing).

entries.name: TextInput — Types
entries.description: Text, password, and email types plus field-level features: tooltip, required, optional, description, disabled, and loading.

entries.name: Text — Truncation
entries.description: Single-line and multi-line text truncation with ellipsis using maxLines in a width-constrained container.

entries.name: Text — Types
entries.description: All 5 semantic text types (body, large, label, supporting, code) with their default styling from the theme.

entries.name: Text — Weight
entries.description: The 4 font weight variants (normal, medium, semibold, bold) applied to body text.

entries.name: Text — Word Break
entries.description: Compares break-word and break-all word break modes on a long unbreakable string.

entries.name: Text — Wrap
entries.description: The 4 text-wrap modes (wrap, nowrap, balance, pretty) shown in width-constrained containers.

entries.name: Theme — Apply Theme
entries.description: Wrap a subtree in Theme to apply a theme to every child component in that region.

entries.name: Theme — Nested Theme
entries.description: Nested Theme providers let a local region use a different theme without affecting the rest of the page.

entries.name: Theme — Distinct Themes

entries.name: Theme — Switch Themes
